title: From a device-tree line to a working driver

steps.title: Seven steps from text to /dev/rtc0
steps.body:
The example is the DS1337 real-time clock on I2C4. Steps 1 to 3 happen on your PC during `./build.sh kernel`; steps 4 to 7 happen on the board at every boot.

Every Linux driver on the board is found and loaded in the same way.

steps.title: 1. A node says what exists and where
steps.body:
In `imx8mp-var-som-symphony.dts` the `rtc@68` node under `&i2c4` has `compatible = "dallas,ds1337"` and `reg = <0x68>`: a DS1337 at I2C address 0x68 on bus I2C4.

The SoC cannot discover this chip by itself, so it has to be written down.

steps.title: 2. dtc turns the text into a binary blob
steps.body:
`dtc` compiles the text into a flat binary tree (an FDT, or "blob"). Includes and overlays are merged here: the SoC and SoM `.dtsi`, the carrier `.dts` and the 1.x revision overlay.

The output is `imx8mp-var-som-1.x-symphony.dtb`.

steps.anchor: 3  Ship it on the SD card
steps.title: 3. The image carries the DTB and the driver module
steps.body:
`image.sh` places `/boot/Image.gz` and the `.dtb` on the card, along with `rtc-ds1307.ko` and `modules.alias` under `/lib/modules/6.18.20-custom/`.

The RTC driver is a module (`=m`), so it is **not** inside the kernel image.

steps.title: 4. U-Boot loads the DTB and passes it in x0
steps.body:
U-Boot runs `load mmc 1:1 ${fdt_addr} /boot/${fdt_file}` with `fdt_addr = 0x4300_0000`, then `booti`. When the kernel starts, register `x0` holds the DTB address.

U-Boot also patches in the RAM size and bootargs under `/chosen`.

steps.title: 5. The kernel makes a device per node
steps.body:
`of_platform` parses the DTB, and the built-in I2C4 driver creates a device for each child node, here `/sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0068` (Linux bus 3 is I2C4, address 0x68).

It has a `modalias` of `of:NrtcT(null)Cdallas,ds1337` but no driver yet.

steps.title: 6. The modalias is looked up in modules.alias
steps.body:
`depmod` builds `modules.alias`, which maps `of:N*T*Cdallas,ds1337` to `rtc_ds1307`. A built-in driver probes at once; a module must be loaded from userspace.

Alpine uses `/sbin/coldplug` with `mdev -d`, Debian uses `systemd-udevd`. Without either, there is no RTC.

steps.title: 7. probe() registers /dev/rtc0
steps.body:
The driver's `of_device_id` table contains `"dallas,ds1337"`. The strings match, `ds1307_probe()` talks to the chip and registers `/dev/rtc0` and `/sys/class/rtc/rtc0`.

`hwclock -u` then works.

steps.anchor: The key is the compatible string: the same text appears in the device tree and in the driver's of_match_table. Change the DT node, and Linux binds a different driver.
steps.title: Takeaway: the compatible string is the key
steps.body: The same text appears in the device tree and in the driver's `of_match_table`. Change the node, and Linux binds a different driver.
